question.text: For hedge accounting to be applied, an entity must, at minimum, identify its:

answer.text: Historical P&L from the hedged position
Risk management objective and how the derivative helps meet it
Total notional value of all derivatives

explanation.text: The Logic: To apply hedge accounting, an entity must identify its risk management objective, demonstrate how the derivative helps meet that objective, specify measurement methods, and document this assessment at inception and periodically. The Trap: Historical P&L, total notional, and trading volume are NOT minimum requirements for hedge accounting designation. The focus is on prospective risk management effectiveness. Cross-Exam Context: Hedge accounting requirements are tested in Series IV and are critical for companies wanting to reduce P&L volatility from hedging activities. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Documentation at inception is crucial — you cannot retroactively designate a derivative as a hedge. The hedge relationship must be formally documented before the transaction begins.
